Translation of Letter from Railway Police Headquarters.

December 23, 1931.

Shanghai Municipal Police,
Shanghai.

Sirs,

With reference to our previous letter requesting
your assistance in effecting the re-arrest of one Tung
Tsau Ping (程贊平) who was formerly arrested by you and
handed over to us and he finally effected his escape by
climbing over the wall of the detention room in No. 1
Divisional Office, has been arrested by our Inspector
Lee Ong Tsung (李鴻春) on December 23, and handed over
to the District Court for trial, but the "mauser" pistol
No. 800215 and fifty-six rounds of ammunition stolen by
him have not been recovered. We have to inform you as
above and to request that should these stolen arms come
to your notice, kindly let us know.

Headquarters of Railway Police
(Shanghai-Nanking Line and
Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Line)

Translation of Letter from Railway Police Headquarters.

No. 500. December 1, 1931.

Shanghai Municipal Police,
Shanghai.

Sirs,

In connection with the larceny of two "Mauser" pistols by one Zung Tsan Ping (程贊平) on 31/10/31, you were requested to render assistance in effecting the arrest of the above named culprit and the recovery of the stolen firearms, which later resulted in the arrest of the culprit as well as the recovery of one of the stolen firearms numbered 800996 by the detectives attached to Sinza Police Station. The accused, after being handed over, was sent to No. 1 Division, Nanking, for enquiry with a view to tracing the other firearm, but he succeeded in effecting his escape by climbing over the wall of the cells at about 6 p.m. 21/11/31. Lyoong Kol. Doong (龔國棟), officer in charge No. 1 Division, made a report to the Administrative Bureau to this effect submitting that the officers concerned be reprimanded and that a coolie named Tsaung Ta Sien (莊芝泉) and a prisoner named Hsun; Muh Pah (金克發) are at present detained and brought before the Shanghai District Court for trial.

The escaped prisoner may take refuge in the Settlement, therefore I have to request you to give instructions to your subordinates in order to have him rearrested.

（批：Circular! / Kay / 3/12）

Tau Ching Dien,
Chief of Railway Police for
Nanking-Shanghai Line and
Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Line.

第 500 号。 1931年12月1日。

致：
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
上海。

先生们：

关于程贊平（Zung Tsan Ping）于31年10月31日盗窃两支“毛瑟”手枪一案，曾请贵方协助逮捕上述罪犯并追回被盗枪械。随后，新闸捕房探员成功逮捕了该罪犯，并追回了其中一支编号为800996的被盗枪械。嫌犯被移交后，被送往南京第一分区进行讯问，以便追查另一支枪械，但他于31年11月21日下午6时许通过攀爬牢房墙壁成功逃脱。第一分区主管官员龔國棟（Lyoong Kol. Doong）就此向行政局提交报告，建议对相关警官予以申斥，并称目前一名名为莊芝泉（Tsaung Ta Sien）的苦力和一名名为金克發（Hsun; Muh Pah）的囚犯已被拘留，并将提解至上海地方法院受审。

逃犯可能藏匿于租界内，因此恳请贵方指示下属将其重新逮捕。

（批：通令！ / Kay / 12月3日）

陶慶田（Tau Ching Dien），
沪宁线及
沪杭甬线铁路警察局长。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 2864 File No. ............
Date 2/12/31
SINZA Station,
Date Nov, 27th, 1931.

Subject (in full) Re attached.

Made by D.I. Robinson. Forwarded by ........................................

Sir,
With reference to the attached, enquiries have been made by
the undersigned and it appears to refer to a case of " Assistance
to Railway Police" (File attached).
The two men concerned were handed over by order of the S.S.D.
Court and the pistol returned.
Enquiries made at the Railway Police elicited that the first
accused had "escaped" from the detention room on Saturday 21st inst.
It is significant that neither of the accused had been arraign-
ed before the Shanghai District Court although they were handed
over on 6/11/31.
This appears to be an act of spite against Bah Tsoong Gee as
the proceedings from Sinza Station were quite in order, and It
is hardly likely that he could have had any connection with the
"escape".

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

D. I. (Crime)
Information
J. D. H. Robinson
D.I.

W. Kay
D.O.D.

先生：

关于附件内容，经卑职查询，此事似乎涉及“协助铁路警察”一案（附档案）。
两名相关人员系根据特区法院命令移交，手枪已归还。
向铁路警察方面查询得知，第一名被告于本月21日星期六从拘留室“逃脱”。
值得注意的是，尽管两名被告于31年11月6日被移交，但均未在上海地方法院出庭受审。
这似乎是对 Bah Tsoong Gee（音译）的报复行为，因为新闸捕房的程序完全合规，且他不太可能与此次“逃脱”有任何关联。

SECRET & CONFIDENTIAL
November 23, 1931
CONFIDENTIAL
DRAWER
C/O. J. Loh Li Kwei,

This is to inform you that
arrests were made by D. I. Pai zoong gee
of Suza Station, in the settlement day
before yesterday in connection with
the smuggling of Mausers on the train.
Although three prisoners had committed
several cases of robbery, yet they
were surely released on receiving a
certain amount of money and
at the request of the Chief of
the railway. We sincerely hope
that you will pay your prompt
and careful attention to this
matter.

The traffic office of
Shanghai Nanking Railway
Station.

Translation of a letter from Railway Police
Headquarters of the S.N.R. & S.H.N.R. Lines
dated November 4, 1931

Dear Sir,

we have reported to you that two Mauser
pistols Nos. 500215 & 800826, and 62 rounds of
ammunition were stolen by one named Dzung Tsai Ping
(程贊平) on the morning of October 31 and requested
your help in dealing with the case. As up to present
nothing has been achieved, we beg to renew our request
and have the pleasure to inform you that a reward of
100 dollars has been offered for the recovery of each
of these two weapons.

Chu Ching Dien (朱慶田)
(Chopped) Railway Police Hdqrs. of the
S.N.R. & S.H.N.R. Lines

Special Branch,
Municipal Police Department
International Settlement
Shanghai

Translation of a letter addressed to the Special Branch,
S.M.P. from the Railway Police Headquarters of the S.N.R.
（印：C. & S. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 2864 2. 11. 31.）
October 31, 1931.

To the Special Branch, S.M.P.

We have received a report from our Inspector named
Zung Dien Zung to the effect that he was visited at his
quarters on the morning of October 31, by a distant uncle
named Zung Tsai Ping(程赞平). The latter stated he was
hungry and asked his nephew to buy some food for him.
Inspector Zung complied with the request of his uncle but
was suprised that when he came back his uncle had gone.
It was then discovered that he had stolen two Mauser pistols
numbered 800215 and 800826 and 62 rounds of ammunition.
Inspector Zung immediately went out to search for his uncle
but his efforts were fruitless.

Apart from ordering Inspector Zung to endeavour to
locate Zung Tsai Ping and issuing instructions to our staff
to do the same, we beg to request that your department
will be good enough to assist us in tracing and arresting
Zung Tsai Ping. We beg to state the description of Zung
Tsai Ping as follows :-
東明
Zung Tsai Ping, age 26, native of Tung Min Hsien, Hopeh.
Height, 4'7" or 4'8"; complexion, pale; thin; wears foreign
clothes; hair combed in foreign style(?). Speaks Shanghai
dialect in addition to his native dialect.

Headquarters of the Railway Police of S.N.R.
and S.H.N.R.

P.A. (for Mr.)
Kenneth Gynn
（批：9/11 2:11:31.）

铁路警察总局致上海公共租界工部局警务处特别支部的信函译文
（印：C. & S. 登记处 S. B. D. 第 2864 号 31年11月2日。）
1931年10月31日。

致：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别支部

我方收到名为钟殿忠（Zung Dien Zung，音译）的督察的报告，称10月31日上午，其远房叔父程赞平（Zung Tsai Ping）到访其寓所。后者称其饥饿，并请侄子为其购买食物。钟督察满足了叔父的请求，但回来时惊讶地发现叔父已离开。随后发现他偷走了两支编号为800215和800826的毛瑟手枪及62发子弹。钟督察立即外出搜寻其叔父，但徒劳无功。

除命令钟督察尽力 locating 程赞平并指示我局职员同样行事外，恳请贵部门协助追踪并逮捕程赞平。现将程赞平的特征描述如下：
東明
程赞平，26岁，籍贯河北东明县。
身高4英尺7英寸或4英尺8英寸；面色苍白；消瘦；穿西装；头发梳成西式发型(?)。除家乡话外，还会说上海话。

沪宁铁路
及沪杭甬铁路警察总局

P.A. (代先生)
Kenneth Gynn
（批：9/11 2:11:31.）
